## Context

DSO's LLM code review pipeline produces multi-cycle PRs that fail to converge. Empirical evidence (PR #65 escalated to user after 4 rounds with explicit "findings have not converged"; PR #62 oscillated 8->8->6 across 3 rounds; ~10-12 of ~50 post-feature PRs took >2 cycles; admin-merge-with-failure on #45 and #65) traces to four interlocking architectural causes: reviewers stateless across cycles, broken CI/local prompt parity, mid-resolution tier ratcheting that introduces fresh-perspective findings, and lack of a structured terminator for sustained disagreement. This epic ships statefulness, parity, arbitration, and tier-decoupling so reframing-oscillation and local-vs-CI divergence stop driving cycle counts.

## User Experience Change

After this ships, a developer running `/dso:review` on a PR that had findings in cycle N will see each cycle-N+1 finding tagged NEW_INTRODUCED, NEW_PRE_EXISTING, RESUSTAIN_OF, or REFRAME_OF — making it immediately visible whether the reviewer is introducing a new concern or re-raising a prior one. CI llm-review will load the same agent prompt files as local `/dso:review`, so findings that pass locally will not silently fail in CI. When a previously defended finding is re-raised, an opus arbiter resolves it within the same review run (sustain, accept defense, or downgrade severity) instead of escalating to the user after MAX_ATTEMPTS. Current state: 10-12 of every ~50 PRs take >2 cycles; target: <5% post-ship.

## Success Criteria

1. **Stateful re-review with reviewer self-declared relations and orchestrator-side verification.** Cycle-N+1 reviewer dispatches receive `prior_findings.json` and `defenses[]` in a `STATEFUL_REVIEW_CONTEXT` block injected only when `prior_findings` is non-empty (cycle N>=2) — first-cycle reviewers carry no additional schema load. The reviewer schema requires per-finding `relation` (one of: NEW_INTRODUCED, NEW_PRE_EXISTING, RESUSTAIN_OF, REFRAME_OF) and (when relation references a prior finding) `prior_finding_id`. Schema and rules live in a new contract file `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-findings-schema.md` (created in Phase 2). The reviewer must complete its diff review before reading `defenses[]` (sequential gate in the prompt: defenses are presented in a delimited section that follows a `--- COMPLETE INITIAL REVIEW ABOVE THIS LINE ---` marker). Auto-downgrade rule: findings with `relation: NEW_PRE_EXISTING` (lines unchanged since cycle N) auto-downgrade to `minor` UNLESS the referenced `prior_finding_id` was previously rated `important` or `critical` (re-elevation of previously-minor findings is prohibited without explicit `ESCALATE_REVIEW`). NEW_INTRODUCED (lines in cycle-N fix delta) are unrestricted to catch fix-induced regressions. **Orchestrator-side verification (RESUSTAIN escape-hatch guard)**: after each reviewer dispatch, the orchestrator computes line-range overlap between each new finding's `cited_lines` and every entry in `prior_findings.json`. If overlap exists and the reviewer declared `NEW_INTRODUCED` without an explicit `escape_rationale` field referencing the prior finding, the orchestrator rejects the relation classification and re-dispatches the reviewer with the message "Finding overlaps prior finding `<id>`; re-classify as RESUSTAIN_OF, REFRAME_OF, or provide explicit escape_rationale."

2. **Single source of truth for review prompts (CI parity, scoped to prompt content).** `plugins/dso/scripts/dso_ci_review/dispatch.py`'s hardcoded 5-line `_SYSTEM_PROMPT` is removed. CI loads the same `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-*.md` agent files used by `/dso:review` and injects them as the `litellm.completion()` system prompt. CI uses `review-complexity-classifier.sh` (with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` bootstrap added to ci.yml — verified by a smoke-test CI step before classifier.py removal), the same overlay dispatch logic (parallel litellm calls per overlay flag), the same schema validation (write-reviewer-findings.sh equivalent), and the same severity rubric and NOT-flag rules from `reviewer-base.md`. **Explicit scope decision**: Phase 1 parity is "same prompts via litellm" — NOT "same Agent-tool dispatch architecture." The deep-tier opus arch synthesis in CI is approximated by a single opus litellm call with `deep-arch.md` as system prompt operating on the merged sonnet specialist outputs (which themselves run as 3 parallel litellm calls). This approximation is documented in `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/ci-vs-local-parity-scope.md`. CI delta from local is limited to: (a) the existing `REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci` injection from closed epic 6da2-4cff, (b) worktree-vs-CI artifact path resolution, (c) Agent-tool-vs-litellm dispatch (now documented). Local-passes-CI-fails as a structural class is eliminated for prompt-content reasons; remaining differences are explicit and documented.

3. **DefenseStore with split backends, shared loader/writer, ticket-binding integrity, and explicit ordering contract.** A shared `DefenseStore` interface has two backends: `TrackerDefenseStore` (writes to ticket comments — used by `/dso:review`) and `GitHubPRDefenseStore` (writes to PR comments — used by CI). Both serialize the same record shape: `prior_finding_id`, `cited_lines_fingerprint`, `defense_text` (max 4096 chars), `defender`, `cycle_number`, `timestamp`, optional `arbiter_ruling` (full arbiter output stored only in TrackerDefenseStore; GitHubPRDefenseStore stores a 1-2 sentence summary with a link to the tracker record). Schema and storage at `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md`. **Ticket-binding integrity**: local review without a session-bound ticket fails with exit code 1 and stderr containing the literal string `ticket-binding required` (test location: `tests/review/test-defense-store-ticket-binding.sh`). When a session has multiple bound tickets (worktree with epic + in-progress story), DefenseStore writes to the most-recently-active story (or epic if no story); the bound ticket ID is written into each defense record so the loader can read across tickets. **`cited_lines_fingerprint` is computed by the orchestrator, not the reviewer**: SHA-256 of the concatenation of `<path>:<line_number>:<whitespace-collapsed-line-content>` for each cited line; whitespace-only formatting changes preserve the fingerprint, semantic edits change it. **Mirror-at-PR-open ordering contract**: a dedicated `mirror-defenses-to-pr` workflow step runs as a `needs:` dependency before `llm-review` in ci.yml; it idempotently posts all tracker defenses for the PR's tickets as PR comments before the first CI review dispatch. Soft fallback: `GitHubPRDefenseStore.load()` falls through to `TrackerDefenseStore` if the mirror has not run (logged warning, accept imperfect statefulness on first CI cycle rather than fail). **Fork-PR fallback**: `GitHubPRDefenseStore.write()` detects `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=pull_request` with head_repo != base_repo and downgrades to no-op with logged warning; CI reviewers on fork PRs read from `TrackerDefenseStore` only (no PR-side persistence). **Bidirectional load on local**: `/dso:review` reads from TrackerDefenseStore by default but ALSO reads from GitHubPRDefenseStore when run against a branch with an open PR — so post-PR-open local cycles see CI-written defenses.

4. **Opus arbiter with trinary authority, anti-compromise discipline, and durable fingerprint binding.** When a finding ID `X` is defended in cycle N (defense recorded in store) and re-raised in cycle N+1 by the reviewer (relation: RESUSTAIN_OF X), the orchestrator dispatches a single opus arbiter (new agent file: `plugins/dso/agents/code-reviewer-arbiter.md`). Inputs: the finding, the defense, the cited diff hunks, the `reviewer-base.md` severity rubric and NOT-flag rules. Trinary output: `SUSTAIN_AT_SEVERITY` (uphold reviewer), `ACCEPT_DEFENSE` (dismiss), or `DOWNGRADE_TO_<severity>` (real concern, lower severity than reviewer asserted). **Anti-compromise instruction in arbiter prompt**: "`DOWNGRADE_TO` is NOT a compromise mechanism. It is for cases where the reviewer's severity is specifically too high but the underlying concern is real. If you find yourself selecting `DOWNGRADE_TO` because you are uncertain between `SUSTAIN_AT_SEVERITY` and `ACCEPT_DEFENSE`, you MUST select `ACCEPT_DEFENSE` instead — uncertainty about the defense's validity is not evidence for the reviewer's severity claim." Arbiter must emit a one-sentence cited_lines-backed rationale for every `DOWNGRADE_TO`. The decision is recorded as a defense record with `arbiter: true` and `cited_lines_fingerprint` snapshotted at decision time. **Durable binding scoped to fingerprint**: subsequent cycles must not re-raise this ID against this code state. If the cited lines change in a later cycle, the reviewer's NEW_INTRODUCED authority applies (with overlap-rationale per SC1) and produces a fresh finding with a fresh ID. Whitespace-only formatting changes preserve the binding; semantic edits release it. Auto-format/import-sort regressions on a previously-arbitrated region are an accepted constraint — the reviewer can flag them as NEW_INTRODUCED with rationale.

5. **Tier upgrade decoupled from cycle-attempt count, including HUGE workflow.** Tier upgrades occur exclusively on explicit `ESCALATE_REVIEW` from the resolution sub-agent (intent gap, scope drift, classifier-base mismatch evidence). The `PASS_NUM>=2` light->standard ratchet (REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md — anchor: the conditional block beginning `if [ "${REVIEW_PASS_NUM}" -ge 2 ]` near the "tier escalation" section) and the MAX_ATTEMPTS->deep upgrade (anchor: the post-loop block immediately following `MAX_ATTEMPTS exceeded`) are removed. **REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md FALLBACK dispatch is reviewed for ratchet patterns** and updated to match the ESCALATE_REVIEW-only escalation model, or the divergence is documented with explicit rationale. `review.max_resolution_attempts` is retained as a backstop. **New exit path** for the case where reviewer cycles through NEW_PRE_EXISTING/NEW_INTRODUCED without RESUSTAIN_OF and the resolution sub-agent exhausts attempts: orchestrator emits `ESCALATE_REVIEW: oscillation_no_arbiter_engagement` (the orchestrator's overlap-rationale check from SC1 will normally have caught this; this is the safety net) and routes to user escalation. Test: an automated regression test asserts (a) tier stays at initial value across 2+ resolution cycles with no ESCALATE_REVIEW signal; (b) ast-grep/grep scan confirms ratchet logic is absent from REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md after Phase 2.

6. **Migration via best-effort file-path binding, with fixture-based validation.** A migration script scans the repo for `# REVIEW-DEFENSE:` source comments (currently 154 instances per audit), extracts each into a defense record bound to its containing file's primary owning ticket (determined by querying which open epic's stories most recently touched that file path; ambiguous or unbindable cases are written with `ticket: UNBOUND` and surfaced in the migration audit log). Records are written to `TrackerDefenseStore` (for bound cases) or to a top-level "Legacy REVIEW-DEFENSE corpus" ticket (for UNBOUND cases). Inline comments are deleted in a single atomic commit. The reviewer-base.md REVIEW-DEFENSE Evaluation section (anchor: section heading `## REVIEW-DEFENSE Evaluation` or equivalent — content-anchor, not line number) and review-fix-dispatch.md inline-comment guidance are removed in the same commit. Migration cutover protocol: communicate cutover date; pre-cutover, both old (inline) and new (DefenseStore) mechanisms are honored; post-cutover, only DefenseStore is read; CLAUDE.md is updated atomically. **Validation (fixture-based)**: PR #65 and PR #62 diffs are checked into `tests/fixtures/review-convergence/<pr-id>.diff` along with a recorded prior-cycle findings JSON; the test harness runs the new pipeline against each fixture and asserts (a) RESUSTAIN_OF X with overlap triggers exactly one arbiter dispatch on the same finding ID, (b) NEW_INTRODUCED on overlapping lines without escape_rationale is rejected and re-dispatched, (c) NEW_PRE_EXISTING auto-downgrades unless prior was important+. **Easy-path regression check**: 5 SHA-pinned single-cycle PRs from the last 90 days are checked in as fixtures; the new pipeline must produce equivalent findings (modulo new relation fields) and remain single-cycle. **Forward-looking validation**: for the 30 days post-ship, P90 cycle_count from `review-stats.sh` is monitored against the pre-ship baseline (recorded at migration commit time); target P90 <= 2 cycles.

## Approach

**Sequential implementation in three phases (Option B from brainstorm).** Each phase is shippable independently with its own PR(s) under the per-story PR size budget.

**Phase 1 — CI parity scoped to prompt content (SC2).** Rewrite `dso_ci_review/dispatch.py` to load `code-reviewer-*.md` files. Bootstrap `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` in ci.yml. Smoke-test `review-complexity-classifier.sh` in CI before removing classifier.py. Document the dispatch-architecture delta in the parity-scope contract. Phase 1 layers on top of in-flight 2fa0-a2d9 (context-augmentation loop); coordinate merge order — 2fa0 ships first, then this Phase 1 layers parity on top. No semantic changes to review behavior.

**Phase 2 — Statefulness, arbitration, tier-decoupling (SC1, SC3-tracker, SC4, SC5).** Add the relation taxonomy and STATEFUL_REVIEW_CONTEXT block to `reviewer-base.md`. Implement `DefenseStore` interface + `TrackerDefenseStore` backend. Implement orchestrator-side overlap verification + escape-rationale gate. Update reviewer dispatch prompts (sequential gate: review diff before reading defenses). Add `code-reviewer-arbiter.md` agent and orchestrator dispatch logic for RESUSTAIN_OF defended IDs. Update REVIEW-WORKFLOW.md and REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md to remove cycle-count tier ratchets. Local stays on tracker backend.

**Phase 3 — PR backend, mirror, migration (SC3-PR, SC6).** Implement `GitHubPRDefenseStore` with fork-PR fallback. Implement mirror-at-PR-open workflow step + soft fallback. Run the one-shot migration commit. Validate against fixtures (PR #65, PR #62, 5 small PRs). Begin 30-day forward-looking telemetry.

## Dependencies

- **Supersedes b6e9-6f1d** ("Reviewer override discipline: defense citations, downgrade quorum, isolation-ok registry"). Both target REVIEW-DEFENSE self-attestation; this epic's structured DefenseStore + arbiter is the more comprehensive replacement. b6e9-6f1d's downgrade-quorum and isolation-ok-registry concepts are subsumed by the orchestrator-side overlap verification (SC1) and the arbiter's binding ruling (SC4). On approval, b6e9-6f1d is closed as superseded with a comment linking here.
- **Depends on 2fa0-a2d9** ("CI context-augmentation loop, prompt caching, turn-budget exhaustion"). Phase 1 parity requires dispatch.py to support multi-turn dispatch (already in 2fa0-a2d9) before loading agent files as system prompts. 2fa0-a2d9 ships first; Phase 1 layers on top.
- **Coordinates with 5018-64ce** ("Evaluate and resolve current TODO/FIXME/HACK and REVIEW-DEFENSE comments"). Our SC6 migration is the authoritative REVIEW-DEFENSE removal path; 5018-64ce defers its REVIEW-DEFENSE slice. SC6's migration script is idempotent against any prior partial removal.
- **Layers on closed epic 6da2-4cff** (severity calibration, NOT-flag rules, REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci marker, cited_lines field). New schema fields (relation, prior_finding_id, cited_lines_fingerprint) coexist in distinct sections from 6da2-4cff's additions. STATEFUL_REVIEW_CONTEXT is conditionally injected and does not conflict with REVIEW_CONTEXT: ci.
- **Coordinates with f61f-7e0a** (Per-Story PR Review Structure) — independent and parallel. The `DefenseStore` interface includes `load_for_region(region_files)` from day 1 (no-op default); region scoping activates if/when f61f-7e0a's Strategy E ships region-split.

## Cross-Epic Interactions

- **Resource: reviewer-base.md and code-reviewer-*.md.** Layers on 6da2-4cff (closed - severity rubric / NOT-flag / cited_lines). New schema sections (relation, STATEFUL_REVIEW_CONTEXT, defense-loader guidance) MUST coexist without colliding with severity/NOT-flag headings. Gate: build-review-agents.sh produces all 10 agents with all required sections after merge.
- **Resource: dso_ci_review/dispatch.py.** Coordination with 2fa0-a2d9 (open - context-augmentation loop). Hard ordering: 2fa0-a2d9 ships first; Phase 1 layers parity on top. Gate: dispatch.py post-Phase-1 must pass 2fa0-a2d9's acceptance tests.
- **Resource: review-fix-dispatch.md and resolution loop.** Resolution sub-agent must consume DefenseStore via Bash CLI (`.claude/scripts/dso review-defense-write` or equivalent) — NOT a nested Task dispatch (per CLAUDE.md rule 17 NESTING PROHIBITION). Gate: Step 3 "Defend findings" instruction in review-fix-dispatch.md is updated atomically with Phase 2 to specify the bash-tool write mechanism. L82 minor-defense prohibition is retained.
- **Resource: oscillation-check skill.** Stable finding IDs and orchestrator-side overlap verification subsume the literal-diff-reversal check oscillation-check performs today. Gate: assess deprecation in implementation plan; until decided, both checks run.
- **Resource: REVIEW-WORKFLOW-HUGE.md.** SC5 explicitly covers HUGE workflow tier-ratchet review. If f61f-7e0a Strategy E ships region-split, the DefenseStore interface's `load_for_region` activates; the interface ships from day 1 with a no-op default to avoid future schema migration.
- **Resource: ci.yml workflow.** New `mirror-defenses-to-pr` step + CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT bootstrap are additive. Coordinate with any other in-flight ci.yml edits at merge time.

## Open Questions for Implementation Plan

- Format of `escape_rationale` field (free-text, structured enum, or both) — implementation-plan task with the orchestrator overlap-verification spec.
- Whether to gate non-arbiter resolution sub-agent dispatches on receiving DefenseStore reads, or treat reads as best-effort.
- Exact storage location for the "Legacy REVIEW-DEFENSE corpus" ticket (new dedicated ticket, or appended to a meta-tracking ticket).
- Whether the orchestrator-side overlap verification should also run in CI (where re-dispatch retries cost API calls).
